summary: Korčula — a walled medieval town often called 'little Dubrovnik' — anchors the southern half of Croatia's island lattice. It bridges the gap between the Split charter cluster and Dubrovnik, with protected channel hops to Mljet (a forested national-park island), remote Lastovo, Hvar and the Pelješac peninsula. Croatia's world-top yachting status and 226 nautical-tourism ports underpin demand, while a growing charter base and dense seasonal catamaran service (Krilo, Jadrolinija) prove the market. Every core leg sits inside Pioneer II range; the sheltered southern channels make for calm, premium-priced island-hopping that completes the Split↔Dubrovnik Dalmatian corridor.
tagline: The southern bridge of the Dalmatian chain — protected channels linking Split and Dubrovnik via Mljet and Lastovo.
